181: A is correct because Amazon SQS decouples the data producers from the data consumers, allowing each microservice to process work asynchronously and scale independently. Since data is processed sequentially but the order of results does not matter, a queue buffers messages and lets consumers pull and process them at their own pace, adding elasticity and resilience to the new microservices architecture. SQS is fully managed and is the standard AWS pattern for asynchronous, decoupled communication between microservices.
182: B is correct because RDS Multi-AZ deploys a synchronous standby instance in a separate Availability Zone, so every committed transaction is written to at least two nodes, which minimizes data loss. If the primary instance fails, RDS automatically fails over to the standby, providing the reliability the company needs after its recent outage. Read replicas replicate asynchronously and do not provide synchronous dual-node writes, and a custom EC2 and Lambda replication solution is unmanaged and unreliable.
183: A is correct because hosting static content in S3 and dynamic content with API Gateway and Lambda eliminates server maintenance and patching entirely. Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode instantly and automatically scales both read and write capacity to match user demand with no provisioning to manage. Combined with CloudFront for global delivery, this fully serverless architecture is highly available, unlike the EC2-based options that still require patching and instance management.
184: A is correct because configuring the Lambda function to run in the VPC gives it an elastic network interface with an associated security group, so its traffic can flow through the existing virtual private gateway and Direct Connect connections to reach the on-premises database. The VPC already has connectivity to the data center, so only the function's network placement needs to change. The other options either duplicate connectivity that already exists or are not technically valid for Lambda.
185: B is correct because the ECS task role, specified as the taskRoleArn in the task definition, provides temporary AWS credentials to the containers in the task, allowing the application to make signed calls to Amazon S3. This is the standard, least-privilege way to grant an ECS application access to other AWS services without embedding long-term credentials. Security groups cannot grant IAM permissions, and relaunching instances as an IAM user does not provide the containers proper access.
186: B is correct because Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows SMB file system that can be mounted by multiple EC2 Windows instances across multiple Availability Zones simultaneously. Amazon EFS is designed for Linux workloads over NFS, and EBS volumes cannot be attached to multiple instances at once, so neither meets the shared Windows file system requirement.
187: A is correct because an RDS DB instance in Multi-AZ mode synchronously replicates data to a standby in another Availability Zone and automatically fails over, giving the relational database tier high availability with no manual intervention. D is correct because an ECS cluster with the Fargate launch type runs the containerized application without the company managing any underlying servers, and ECS scales the tasks automatically to handle the dynamic application load. The EC2-based alternatives require provisioning, patching, and managing instances, which increases manual intervention.
188: A is correct because AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed, highly available SFTP-enabled server whose endpoint maps directly to the S3 data lake, so the partner can upload files over SFTP with no servers to run or patch. The managed service handles availability, scaling, and user authentication automatically, minimizing operational overhead. The EC2 and NLB-based options require the company to build and maintain its own SFTP infrastructure and cron-based upload scripts.
189: B is correct because S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents the contract documents from being overwritten or deleted by anyone, including privileged users, for the entire retention period, enforcing the 5-year immutability requirement. D is correct because server-side encryption with a KMS customer managed key supports automatic annual key rotation, which can be configured to meet the yearly rotation requirement. Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permissions, and SSE-S3 keys are not customer controlled and cannot be rotated on a configured schedule.
190: B is correct because Elastic Beanstalk is a managed platform that natively supports Java and PHP web applications, handles provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring, and requires minimal operational overhead. URL swapping between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments lets the company test new site features on an identical environment and quickly switch traffic to it, making frequent testing easy. The EC2 and container-based options require significant management, while an S3 static site with Lambda cannot host this full Java and PHP web application.
191: A is correct because creating a read replica offloads the long-running, one-time reporting queries to a separate instance, leaving the primary DB instance dedicated to order processing so the timeouts are eliminated. Employees can still run their reporting queries at any time against the replica without impacting production traffic. Spreading the ordering application across the primary and replica would not work because replicas are read-only and the application must write orders.
192: B is correct because writing the extracted document information to Amazon S3 provides a highly scalable and durable store, and Amazon Athena provides serverless SQL queries over that data with no infrastructure to manage, satisfying the SQL query requirement. E is correct because a Lambda function triggered on each upload scales automatically with the hundreds of daily documents, and Amazon Textract is the purpose-built service for extracting raw text from scanned documents while Amazon Comprehend Medical is designed to detect and extract relevant medical information. These fully managed services maximize scalability and operational efficiency, whereas the EC2 and MySQL options require managing servers.
193: A is correct because Amazon RDS read replicas offload the high volume of read traffic from the source databases, reducing the read load on each primary instance and scaling read capacity horizontally. Read replicas also enhance availability because a replica can be promoted if the source instance fails, meeting the high-availability requirement. DNS caching does not address database load, and the caching alternatives do not provide the database-level read scaling and availability that read replicas deliver for this batch workload.
194: A is correct because running the database on two EC2 instances in different Availability Zones configured as a cluster with database replication provides automatic failover, so if one instance or AZ experiences a disruptive event the other continues serving the database. This directly meets both the high-availability and automatic failover requirements for the EC2-based database. The other options rely on AMI backups and recovery mechanisms, which involve downtime and do not provide continuous availability or automatic failover.
195: C is correct because sending orders to an Amazon SQS queue decouples the order system from the EC2 instances, so messages are durably persisted even during an outage and are automatically consumed and processed once the instances recover. Users no longer need to reprocess orders because nothing is lost while the system is down. The Auto Scaling group maintains processing capacity, and this queue-based pattern provides resilience without building custom failover logic.
196: D is correct because DynamoDB Time to Live is a native feature that automatically deletes items when a timestamp attribute expires, so adding an attribute with the current timestamp plus 30 days and enabling TTL removes data older than 30 days with no additional infrastructure. This minimizes both cost and development effort because AWS manages the deletion process entirely. The other options require building and running extra components such as Lambda functions, DynamoDB Streams, or EC2 monitoring instances to perform the cleanup.
197: B is correct because rehosting in Elastic Beanstalk on the .NET platform keeps the application largely unchanged while Elastic Beanstalk manages provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring, and Multi-AZ deployment provides high availability. E is correct because AWS DMS can migrate the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS, keeping the same database engine so the application requires minimal changes, and Multi-AZ deployment provides the required availability. Refactoring to Lambda or migrating to DynamoDB would require significant development changes.
198: D is correct because Amazon EKS runs the same Kubernetes environment the company already uses, so no deployment method changes are needed, and AWS Fargate removes the need to manage EC2 worker nodes, minimizing operational overhead. Amazon DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible, which means the application's MongoDB data layer can be migrated without code changes. The ECS and DynamoDB alternatives would require changing the orchestration platform or rewriting the data access layer.
199: B is correct because Amazon Transcribe provides multi-speaker recognition and generates transcript files from the call recordings, which can be stored durably in Amazon S3 for the required 7-year retention period. Amazon Athena then provides serverless, SQL-based analysis of the transcript files stored in S3 to identify business patterns without managing any infrastructure. The other options use Amazon Rekognition, which is for image and video analysis rather than speech, and do not provide the required speaker recognition and transcript analysis.
200: D is correct because an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer in API Gateway is the native integration that lets Amazon Cognito validate each user's identity token on every request, controlling access to the REST API. Since the company already uses Amazon Cognito to manage its users, this AWS-managed solution requires no custom validation code and delivers the least development effort and operational overhead. The Lambda authorizer, API key, and email header options all require building and maintaining custom validation logic.
